title: Inbound leads
brief_markdown:
Chapter 5 was about going out to get appointments. This chapter is about what happens when someone comes to you, and for Myda the honest answer is: not much, unless you build for it. Nobody is googling "AI feedback coach for TikTok Shop creators". Your inbound for the next six months is a by-product of outbound and posting: a Head of E-commerce reads the LinkedIn note, looks at the site, fills in the beta form; a beta tester tells a friend who runs an agency. These are the best leads you will get, because they came off lists you already qualified and raised their own hand. This module is about not wasting them.

### Inbound cuts both ways
A lead who asks for Myda has intent twenty connection requests a day cannot manufacture. Sofia filling in the form at 23:40 with "we get maybe 40 creator videos a month and most of them are unusable" is a buyer describing the problem in the narrative's own words. The catch: she decided she is a fit, not you. She has one content person and no TikTok Shop manager; on the ICP she is borderline. Inbound does not suspend qualification, it moves it to the first reply. The standard stays Module 4's: the account has the pain, the volume of creator video, and someone whose job it is to fix it. A freelancer wanting feedback on his own videos is enthusiastic and unqualified; ten polite minutes beat a three-week beta that fails.

### Make it easy to raise a hand
Today a lead who wants Myda has to find a founder on LinkedIn or guess an email. Fix that first. One big "Join the beta" button on the site, following the reader down the page, pointing at a form that works on a phone, where your LinkedIn messages are read. Ask for the minimum: name, company, role, work email, phone, plus what you cannot find out yourself. A TikTok Shop page shows whether a brand sells in the UK or Germany; it does not show how many creator videos arrive each month or who reviews them tonight. Every extra field loses a lead. Put a phone number on the form and the thank-you page: the agency founder who does business by voice will call rather than type, and a voicemail is a stronger signal than a form. Put the form link in the footer of every outreach email. Discord and LinkedIn DMs are inbound channels too; they just need an owner. No chat widget nobody will staff: a bubble that asks "how can we help?" and goes silent is worse than none.

### Minutes, not days
The chapter's hardest rule: interest decays fast. The research it cites shows contact rates falling roughly a hundredfold between a reply inside five minutes and one at thirty. Sofia is on her phone reviewing creator videos the moment she submits; tomorrow she has joined another waitlist. So the form sends a notification with her phone number to whoever is on point, and that person calls, from wherever they are. Two founders cannot both watch the inbox all day, so split the days. For a lead at 23:40, an auto-reply that says what happens next and gives a number to call bridges the gap, and the call goes out before 09:00. Make the service level a number you can measure from timestamps.

### Qualify the account, not the lead
When you reach her, resist the demo. First, five questions in plain language that verify the ICP: what she sells and where; how many creator videos a month, from how many creators; who reviews them today and what happens to the ones that miss; who would use Myda day to day and who decides on a tool like this; and what would need to be true in three weeks to call the beta a success. Then decide, out loud, one of three outcomes. Strong fit, decision maker on the phone: book the demo now, content person on the call. Borderline on size but strong on pain and volume, like Sofia: a scoped beta with a named success metric, so both sides know what "it worked" means. Not a fit: say so, say why, say who Myda is for, and give a date to check back. People you turn down kindly tell their qualified friends about you; people you demo under false pretences tell everyone else. Watch for the unqualified contact at a qualified account: the intern who filled in the form at a twelve-brand agency is a door, not a dead end. Ask who owns creator quality and get introduced. For leads whose form answers already say no (no TikTok Shop, no creators, outside the US, UK or EU), do not call: send a short email saying who Myda is for, why they may not fit, and asking them to correct you. Often they will.

### Do not stop at one attempt
If the first call goes to voicemail, you have not lost her. Each further attempt adds a real chance of contact; after about six across phone, email and LinkedIn you have had most of the chance you will ever get. Leave a voicemail and send the first-reply email in the same hour, log every attempt, and after six, park the lead and move on. She asked to be contacted; persistence is courtesy, not pestering.

### This week
Agree who owns which inbound source on which days, put the button and form on the site, write the auto-reply, and put the five questions where both of you can read them on a phone. Tag every inbound lead in the CRM with its source from the first row, so Module 8's pipeline can tell inbound from outbound and show which source converts.

### What you build in this module
A shared inbound lead handling artifact: sources and owners, the response-time rule and rota, the five-question qualification script and its three outcomes, website form and auto-reply copy, first-reply templates per source, CRM fields and the inbound tag, weekly inbound metrics.

### Drill
Sofia filled in the beta form at 23:40 last night and left her number. It is 08:50. Call her back.

build.spec_markdown:
Produce {{company}}'s inbound lead handling, section by section, in this order. Work one question at a time; record each section with update_artifact as soon as it is good enough, then move to the next. Pull the fit score, the disqualifiers and the CRM stages from the icp artifact (Module 4) and the FAQ answers, phone-script branches and overview video from the materials artifact (Module 3); do not rewrite them here, reference them.

1. **Sources and owners.** Every inbound source {{company}} has today, one row each: website beta form, replies and comments on LinkedIn posts, LinkedIn DMs, Discord (server joins and messages), event sign-ups, referrals from beta testers, and any other that exists. Per source: where the lead lands (which inbox, which notification), which founder owns it, and how a lead there is noticed within the response-time rule. Push back on "we both watch it"; one name per source.
2. **Response-time rule and rota.** One service level in minutes for leads that arrive in working hours and one deadline for leads that arrive at night or at the weekend (Sofia's 23:40 form is the test case), stated as numbers that can be measured from timestamps. A rota: who is on point on which days, what "on point" means (phone in pocket, form notifications on), and what happens when the on-point founder is in a call. Push back on anything measured in days.
3. **Qualification script.** The five questions, in plain spoken language, that verify the icp artifact's demand signifiers for an inbound lead: what they sell on TikTok Shop and in which markets; how many creator videos a month, from how many creators; who reviews them today and what happens to the ones that miss the brief; who would use {{company}} day to day and who decides on a tool like this; and what would need to be true in three weeks to call the beta a success. Then the fit decision: which answers map to the icp fit score, which answers are disqualifiers (freelancers, no TikTok Shop, no creator videos, outside US/UK/EU, already contacted outbound). Then the three outcomes with the exact condition for each: book a demo now (fit above the icp threshold and the decision maker reachable; the demo is the customised one from the materials artifact, with their content person on the call); scoped beta with a success metric (borderline on size but strong on pain and volume; name the metric, the 3-week window, the two feedback sessions, who attends); polite park (disqualified; the reason said plainly, who {{company}} is for, and a date to check back). Add the rule for the unqualified contact at a qualified account: ask who owns creator quality and get introduced.
4. **Website form and auto-reply.** The form fields, each with a reason it cannot be found on the brand's TikTok Shop page or LinkedIn: name, company, role, work email, phone, plus the demand signifiers (creator videos per month, who reviews them today, markets). The thank-you page copy and the auto-reply email: what happens next and by when, a phone number to call now, the two-minute overview video from the materials artifact. Plus the hard-qualifier email for leads whose form answers already fail a disqualifier: who {{company}} is for, why this lead may not fit, an ask to correct the assumption.
5. **First-reply templates per source**, each with exactly one call to action and the lead's own words from their form or message in the first line: (a) email reply to a form submission; (b) LinkedIn DM reply to a post comment or DM; (c) phone call-back, 60 seconds of bullets plus the branches: reached (run the five questions), voicemail (what to say, and the email sent in the same hour), "is it free during beta?", "we're really small, is this for us?", "can my content person just use it without me?", "do you train on our creators' videos?" (the FAQ answers from the materials artifact, by reference; if the FAQ has no answer, the branch says "I'll confirm in writing today", not an invented policy). Then the follow-up cadence when the first attempt fails: six attempts across phone, email and LinkedIn over how many days, and what happens after the sixth.
6. **CRM fields and the inbound tag.** The fields logged for every inbound lead: source, lead timestamp, first-response timestamp, response time in minutes, fit score from the icp, outcome (demo / scoped beta / parked), success metric if a beta, attempts so far, next step with date and owner. The tag convention (`inbound:<source>` on every row, `outbound` on everything from Module 5) so that Module 8's pipeline can split the two. Which icp stage an inbound lead enters at, per outcome.
7. **Weekly inbound metrics.** The numbers read every Monday and who reads them: leads per source, median first-response time and share inside the rule, share qualified, outcomes split, demos booked, scoped betas started, leads still in the attempt loop, leads parked with a check-back date. One line on what each number should make the founders change if it moves.

Standards to enforce on every section: every rule is a number or a name, never "quickly" or "whoever is free"; every template opens with the lead's own words and has exactly one call to action; every answer to a policy question (price, free beta, training on creator videos) comes from the pricing or materials artifact or is marked `TODO: decide and add to FAQ`, never improvised; the three outcomes have conditions a stranger could apply to Sofia's form and reach the same answer. Push back on a qualification script that is a pitch in disguise and on any outcome that books a demo for a lead the icp artifact would disqualify. Mark the artifact done only when all seven sections exist, the rota has two names on it, and both founders could run the call-back from the artifact alone on a phone screen.

drill.channel: phone call back, the morning after a website beta-form submission at 23:40 (she gave her number)
drill.scenario: Sofia Lindqvist, co-founder of a 4-person skincare brand selling on TikTok Shop UK and Germany, filled in the beta form at 23:40 last night ('we get maybe 40 creator videos a month and most of them are unusable, can we try it?') and left her number. It is 08:50 and you are calling her back as the on-point founder; she is already on her phone going through yesterday's creator videos. Run the five questions from the inbound artifact and qualify her honestly against the ICP: she is borderline on size (no TikTok Shop manager, one content person) and strong on intent and volume. Decide the outcome out loud, a scoped beta with her content person and a named success metric, not a full pitch and not a brush-off, and answer 'is it free?', 'we're really small, is this for us?' and 'do you train on our creators' videos?' from the FAQ without inventing policy. Leave the call with a start date this week and her content person's name; she loses interest within a day if nothing concrete is agreed.
drill.buyer_opening: Hej, Sofia. Oh, {{company}}! That was quick, I only sent that form last night. I'm literally on my phone going through yesterday's creator videos right now, so you've caught me at the right moment. I've got about ten minutes before our stand-up. Is this a proper call or do you just want to know who we are?

rows.criterion: Opened with her form in her own words ('40 creator videos a month, most unusable') and acknowledged when she sent it; did not open with a pitch or a cold-call 'tell me about your company'
Asked at least four of the five qualification questions from the inbound artifact in plain spoken language, before any demo talk or pricing
Qualified the account, not the lead: established who reviews creator videos today, who would use {{company}} day to day (the content person) and who decides (Sofia with her co-founder)
Said the outcome out loud and named it as a scoped beta with a success metric (3 weeks, two feedback sessions, what 'it worked' means in a number); neither a full pitch nor a brush-off
Answered 'is it free?' with the beta offer from the pricing artifact (paid, 50% off for a year for beta testers) without flinching, discounting further or inventing a free tier

Answered 'we're really small, is this for us?' honestly against the ICP: named where she is borderline (no TikTok Shop manager, one content person) and what makes the beta worth it anyway (volume and pain), rather than a reflexive yes
Answered 'do you train on our creators' videos?' from the materials FAQ, or said plainly that he would confirm in writing today; did not improvise a data policy
Left with a start date this week, the content person's name, and one next step with an owner; said what he would send and by when, and stayed inside ten minutes

rubric.below_threshold_note: Below 10: fix the qualification script and the phone call-back template in the inbound artifact before repeating with the same persona. Add every question Sofia asked that the FAQ could not answer (free beta, training on creator videos, content person using it alone) to the materials FAQ with a decided answer. Carry forward the weakest row; if row 4 scored 0, the fix carried forward is 'say the outcome out loud before the call ends'.
